newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen pausing after 31-month high.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen pausing after 31-month high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are set to take a breather on Wednesday after the Hang Seng closed at a 31-month high on Tuesday, with renewed interest rate fears on Wall Street expected to dampen prices, analysts said.

"Given that the rally has been strong, it is quite normal to see some profit-taking and I think the market should take a break and resume its uptrend later," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
The Hang Seng has risen 596 points over the past seven sessions. On Tuesday it closed 53.71 points higher at 11,621.61.
Later the Hang Seng London Reference index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London fell 65.64 to 11,555.97.

An unidentified senior U.S. Federal Reserve official told Reuters on Tuesday eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System had requested a hike in the 5.0 percent discount rate. The U.S. long bond tumbled 30/32 to yield 7.03 percent and Dow industrials slipped 0.37 point to 5,888.83.
"This is going to cause some people to think interest rates might be on the way up after all," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"I think its going to be sideways trading today," he added.
